# Audit backlog

Findings from auditing each change against `README.md` (authoritative), `Arch.md`
and `agents.md`. The auditor only records findings; it does not change code.
Each entry: severity, the commit it was found in, the evidence, and a suggested
resolution. Mark resolved entries `[x]` with the fixing commit.

Severity: **HIGH** = classification/security impact or spec violation,
**MED** = code/doc drift or missing required coverage, **LOW** = hardening.

---

## Audit 1 — `e8d5871`, `04ce80a` (2026-10-29)

Gates: `cargo fmt --check` OK · `cargo build` 0 warnings · `cargo test` 46/46 ·
`cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings` OK.

- [x] **HIGH — Method case-folding reverted; the fall-through bypass is back and is now asserted as expected behaviour** (`04ce80a`) — **resolved in `fc32096`: folding restored. Superseded by Audit 15, because folding alone left the reverse case open; non-uppercase spellings that disagree now return `None`**
  - `normalize::method` (src/normalize.rs:31) no longer upper-cases. With the
    rules in `tests/security.rs`, `classify("delete", "api.acme.com",
    "/v1/charges/ch_1")` returns `payment.read`. `DELETE` returns
    `payment.refund`. `method_matching_is_case_sensitive` now asserts
    `payment.read` for `delete`/`Delete`.
  - That contradicts the module doc at the top of `tests/security.rs`
    ("must not reach a broader, less sensitive rule"). It also contradicts
    `Arch.md:340`, `Arch.md:426`, `Arch.md:464` and `agents.md:61`, which all
    say methods are folded to uppercase.
  - Resolve by picking one policy and making code, tests and both docs agree:
    - (a) Restore folding.
    - (b) Keep case-sensitivity, revert the doc lines, and close the
      fall-through another way. For example, return `None` when the method
      is not all uppercase and a method-specific rule would have matched
      its uppercased form. Or reject non-uppercase methods outright.

    Either way, a test should not assert that `delete` gets the less sensitive
    class.

- [x] **MED — Single-label subdomain restriction contradicts the docs** (`e8d5871`) — **resolved in `8a43772`: multi-label subdomains allowed again, matching `Arch.md:333`**
  - `config.rs` now rejects `subdomain = "api.eu"` (`is_dns_label`).
    `Arch.md:333` says "`*` or one or more valid DNS labels" and cites the
    README.
  - This is fail-closed, so there's no security impact. It's a deliberate
    narrowing of the README's "subdomain followed by host" wording.
  - Resolve by updating `Arch.md:333` back to a single label with a one-line
    rationale (the same host can still be written as `host = "eu.acme.com"`,
    `subdomain = "api"`), or by reverting the restriction.

- [x] **LOW — `CompiledRule::new` still accepts dotted subdomains** (src/matcher.rs, `Some(value) => normalize::host(value)`) — **resolved in `8a43772`: config and matcher both accept DNS names again**
  - Only `config.rs` enforces the one-label rule. `agents.md` asks for one
    canonicalization contract, not checks duplicated per module. If anything
    builds a `CompiledRule` without going through `config::parse`, the two
    disagree.
  - Resolve by enforcing the label rule in the shared helper, or by having
    `CompiledRule::new` take an already-validated subdomain.

## Audit 2 — `80ff741` (2026-10-29)

Gates: `cargo fmt --check` OK · `cargo build` 0 warnings · `cargo test` 46/46 ·
`cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings` OK.

- [x] **HIGH — `//` paths accepted again; the fall-through bypass is now asserted as expected** (`80ff741`) — **resolved in `fc32096` via option (a): `//` rejected. Re-verified in Audit 15: `empty_path_segments_are_unclassified` and `generated_paths_classify_only_when_they_are_unambiguous`**
  - `classify("POST", "api.acme.com", "/v1//refunds/x")` returns
    `payment.read`, but `/v1/refunds/x` returns `payment.refund`.
    `duplicate_path_segments_are_preserved_for_matching` asserts the
    `payment.read` result.
  - Servers that merge slashes (nginx `merge_slashes on` by default, many
    framework routers) execute the refund. The agent gets a refund
    classified as a read.
  - It contradicts `Arch.md:351`, `Arch.md:436`, `agents.md:63` and the
    `tests/security.rs` module doc. The README says "Requests are matched as
    an HTTP client would send them", and the server-side interpretation is
    what makes the action dangerous.
  - Resolve by picking a policy and syncing code, tests and docs:
    - (a) Restore rejection, i.e. return `None`. That is fail-closed, and
      real clients essentially never send `//`.
    - (b) Collapse `//` for both rules and requests.
    - (c) Keep preserving it, but apply the same disagreement check
      already used for trailing slashes: classify the collapsed spelling too
      and return `None` if the classes differ.

    Do not keep a test that asserts the less sensitive class.

- [x] **MED — Quadratic `remove_dot_segments` reintroduced** (src/normalize.rs, `80ff741`) — **resolved in `fc32096`: linear stack version restored. Re-verified in Audit 15: `normalization_stays_linear_well_beyond_the_request_limit`**
  - The `String::drain(..n)` / `replace_range` loop shifts the remaining
    buffer once per segment, so cost is O(segments × length).
  - With the same algorithm at `0ea6f30`, a 64 KB path took about 21 ms
    per `classify` in release, and much longer in debug.
  - That path is attacker-controlled input to an HTTP handler. The linear
    stack version this replaced can keep empty segments: push `""`
    segments instead of rejecting them.
  - At minimum, cap the request path length (e.g. 8 KiB, then `None`) and
    test it.

- [x] **LOW — `//` in patterns is accepted silently** (`pattern_path("/v1//x")`) — **resolved in `fc32096`: `pattern_path("/v1//x")` is `None`. Re-verified in Audit 15: `configured_patterns_follow_the_request_path_rules`**
  - Under the current policy a rule `/v1//x` is legal and distinct from
    `/v1/x`. Whatever HIGH resolution is chosen, patterns should follow the
    same rule as requests: rejected or collapsed in both, not one of each.

## Audit 3 — `8a43772`, `fc32096` (2026-10-29)

Gates: `cargo fmt --check` OK · `cargo build` 0 warnings · `cargo test` 47/47 ·
`cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings` OK.

These commits restore the documented policies (multi-label subdomains,
upper-case method folding, `//` rejection, linear dot-segment removal). Code,
tests, `Arch.md` and `agents.md` agree again on all Audit 1/2 items.

- [x] **LOW — Redundant assertion in `method_case_does_not_fall_through_to_method_less_rule`** (tests/security.rs) — **resolved in `09a4754`**
  - The standalone `DELETE` assertion duplicates the first iteration of the
    loop that follows. It's harmless; drop it for clarity.

- [x] **LOW — Policy churn is visible in history** (`04ce80a` → `fc32096`, `e8d5871` → `8a43772`, `80ff741` → `fc32096`) — **resolved in `943c586`: Arch.md §7/§9 record the rationale for each final policy. The history itself stays visible, so be ready to discuss it**
  - Three policies were reverted and then restored within ten minutes.
    Reviewers will read the history and transcript. Be ready to explain
    the decision for each, or record the rationale in Arch.md §7/§9 so the
    final state reads as deliberate.

## Audit 4 — `61aa677` (2026-10-29)

Gates: `cargo fmt --check` OK · `cargo build` 0 warnings · **`cargo test`
FAILS: 5 failures** · `cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings` OK.

- [x] **HIGH — Two README starter tests fail; the deliverable gate is broken** (`61aa677`, src/lib.rs `classify`) — **resolved in `c2e2283`: an unclassified alternative spelling no longer counts as disagreement; 4/4 example tests pass**
  - The trailing-slash check is now symmetric and treats "the other spelling
    is unclassified" as a disagreement. So every exact rule is denied unless
    the opposite-slash spelling is also covered by a rule with the same class.
  - Failing tests:
    - `example.rs`: `exact_rule_matches` (`GET api.acme.com
      /v1/payment_intents` → `None`, expected `payment.read`) and
      `rule_without_subdomain_applies_to_the_host_itself` (`/pricing` →
      `None`).
    - `classification.rs`: `most_specific_rule_wins` and
      `host_patterns_respect_label_boundaries`.
    - `conflicts.rs`: `same_class_duplicates_are_harmless`.
  - README deliverable 1 requires `cargo test` to pass, and `agents.md`
    says to keep the four example tests passing.

- [x] **HIGH — Specific rules under a broader wildcard become unreachable** (same change) — **resolved in `5b59802`: one-way check restored; `/v1/msg/send` and `/v1/payouts` classify again; Arch.md:437 and agents.md:63 updated**
  - Even if `None` alternatives were ignored, a symmetric check denies any
    narrower rule nested under a wildcard. With `/v1/*/send` →
    `communication.external.send` and `/v1/*` → `payment.read`, the request
    `/v1/msg/send` is denied, because `/v1/msg/send/` matches only `/v1/*`.
    The same happens to the test file's `/v1/payouts` → `payment.create`
    rule, which `trailing_slash_that_changes_the_class_is_unclassified` now
    asserts as `None`.
  - That is fail-closed, so it isn't a bypass. But it silently disables
    ordinary configurations, and README-style rule sets stop working.
  - Recommended resolution: revert to the one-directional check from
    `8a7f3ae`:
    - only when the request ends in `/`, also classify the stripped
      spelling;
    - deny only if that is `Some` and different.

    Rationale: the path as sent is authoritative. The ambiguity worth
    guarding is servers *stripping* a trailing slash, while servers adding
    one is rare (redirects aside, which go through classification again).
    If symmetric checking is wanted anyway, document it in Arch.md §9 and
    update all five affected tests. Expect to justify why README examples
    no longer classify.

## Audit 5 — `497f84f` (2026-10-29)

Gates: `cargo fmt --check` OK · `cargo build` 0 warnings · **`cargo test`
still FAILS: the same 5 failures as Audit 4** (the new tests pass) ·
`cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings` OK.

The bounded overlap check fits Arch.md §13: "reject potentially conflicting
patterns with an explicit error" rather than accept an unresolved ambiguity.
The 1M-state cap is checked with `checked_add`/`checked_mul` before
allocating, and the flat `Vec<bool>` replaces nested vectors. Both new tests
pass.

- [x] **LOW — Identical patterns are reported as "too complex" instead of as a conflict** (src/matcher.rs `globs_overlap`) — **resolved in `98788f4`: `left == right` short-circuits before the budget**
  - Two rules with the same 1,000-`*` path and different classes are
    trivially a conflict. They get `ConflictAnalysisTooComplex`, which
    points the user at the wrong problem.
  - Short-circuit `left == right` (and `None`/`None`) to `Ok(true)` before the
    size check.

- [x] **LOW — The cap is per pair, with no total budget** (`find_conflict`) — **addressed in `b2d8402`, but it overcorrects; see Audit 6 MED**
  - Load cost is up to `n² × 1M` states when many long equal-specificity
    wildcard rules share a host and method. Config is user-supplied and
    `load` runs in an HTTP handler (README), so a large set could stall a
    worker.
  - Consider a pattern-length limit at validation (e.g. 2 KiB) or a total
    state budget across all pairs. Note it in Arch.md §16.

- [x] **LOW — New `LoadError` variant isn't documented** (Arch.md §14 lists error categories) — **resolved in `98788f4`: Arch.md §14 lists `ConflictAnalysisTooComplex` and `TooManyRules`**
  - Add "conflict analysis too complex" next to "Conflicting rules" so the
    docs match the public enum.

- Still open: both Audit 4 HIGH items. `tests/classification.rs` and the new
  `tests/robustness.rs` were being edited during this audit and will be
  audited once committed.

## Audit 6 — `c2e2283`, `b2d8402` (2026-10-29)

Gates (each commit checked separately; `c2e2283` from a clean export):
`cargo fmt --check` OK · `cargo build` 0 warnings · `cargo test` 51/51 at
`c2e2283`, 52/52 at `b2d8402` · `cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings` OK.

- [x] **HIGH (carried from Audit 4) — Nested-wildcard rules unreachable, now asserted by a test** (src/lib.rs `classify`, tests/classification.rs `most_specific_rule_wins`) — **resolved in `5b59802`: one-way check restored; `/v1/msg/send` and `/v1/payouts` classify again; Arch.md:437 and agents.md:63 updated**
  - The check is still symmetric. `GET api.acme.com/v1/msg/send`, with
    rule `/v1/*/send` → `communication.external.send`, now returns `None`,
    and the test expects `None`. Any narrower rule under a broader wildcard
    is unreachable unless the narrow pattern also matches the slash-appended
    form.
  - It is fail-closed, so not a bypass. But a reviewer reading
    `most_specific_rule_wins` will see that "most specific wins" fails in an
    ordinary case. README: "When several rules match a request, the most
    specific wins."
  - Arch.md:437 describes only the `/x/` → `/x` direction, not appending a
    slash.
  - Resolve with the one-directional check from Audit 4 (only strip the
    slash from a request that ends in `/`). Otherwise document the
    symmetric rule and its cost in Arch.md §9 and name this trade-off in
    the test.

- [x] **MED — Pair-check cap limits every load to about 447 rules in total** (`b2d8402`, src/matcher.rs `find_conflict`) — **resolved in `98788f4`: the pair cap was replaced by a total state budget charged only to eligible pairs. See Audit 11 for a new MED in its place**
  - `checked_pairs` counts every pair before any filtering. 448 rules fail
    to load even when they are all disjoint: different hosts, same class,
    or different specificity. A realistic deployment that loads several
    provider mapping sets could reach this and get
    `ConflictAnalysisTooComplex`.
  - That error names an arbitrary pair that has nothing to do with the
    cause, which is misleading.
  - Resolve by counting only pairs that reach the expensive step (different
    class, equal specificity, overlapping method and host). Or group rules
    by host pattern and specificity first, so only same-group pairs are
    compared. Or replace both caps with one total budget of glob-overlap
    states. Document the limit in Arch.md §14/§16.

- [x] **LOW — `same_class_duplicates_are_harmless` was weakened** (`c2e2283`, tests/conflicts.rs) — **resolved in `09a4754`: `/x` restored**
  - The rule changed from `/x` to `/x*`, apparently to get past the
    trailing-slash failure that `c2e2283` itself then fixed. The test no
    longer covers exact duplicate rules.
  - Restore `/x`; it passes with the current `classify`.

- [x] **LOW — Robustness generator rarely produces valid input** (tests/robustness.rs) — **resolved in `db5a4c7`: 80% of generated requests are valid, with an assertion that at least 500 of 2,000 classify and that results are in `ACTION_CLASSES`**
  - Hosts are random strings from a 15-character alphabet, so almost none
    parse as `*.acme.com`. Nearly every iteration exits at host
    normalization, and the matcher, glob and trailing-slash code is barely
    exercised.
  - The determinism and order-independence assertions therefore mostly
    compare `None` to `None`.
  - Bias the generator: choose the host from a small valid set (e.g.
    `api.acme.com`, `x.acme.com`, `acme.com`), build the path from valid
    segments, then mutate. Also assert that the result is `None` or a
    member of `ACTION_CLASSES` (Arch.md §17).

## Audit 7 — `5b59802` (2026-10-29)

Gates (clean export): `cargo fmt --check` OK · `cargo build` 0 warnings ·
`cargo test` 52/52 · `cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings` OK.

Code, tests, Arch.md §9 and agents.md now agree on the one-way trailing-slash
rule. No new findings. Open after this audit: MED pair-check cap (Audit 6),
plus the LOW items.

## Audit 8 — `4b49f06` (2026-10-29)

Gates (re-run from a clean export; the first run accidentally included
uncommitted `7235e08` work): `cargo fmt --check` OK · `cargo build` 0 warnings · `cargo test` 52/52 ·
`cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings` OK. Arch.md §9 and agents.md were
updated together with the code.

Rejecting an all-numeric final label closes the IPv4 short forms (`127.1`,
`010.0.0.1`, `1.2.3.4.5`) that `Ipv4Addr::from_str` misses. This is
consistent with "Reject unsupported IP literal representations".

- [x] **LOW — Numeric exact subdomains can no longer be configured** (src/config.rs subdomain validation → `normalize::host`) — **resolved in `2907b0d`: the combined host is validated**
  - Subdomain validation reuses `normalize::host`, where a bare label is its
    own "final label". So `subdomain = "123"` and `subdomain = "api.1"` now
    fail to load, although `123.acme.com` is an ordinary DNS name.
  - Probe: `subdomain = "123"` loads → `false`. The request `123.acme.com`
    still classifies through `subdomain = "*"`, so this is only a config
    restriction (fail-closed).
  - Resolve by applying the numeric-final-label check to the *combined*
    host (`subdomain.host`), or to request and base hosts only. Validate
    subdomains with the DNS-label rules alone.

- [x] **LOW — Hex IPv4 forms still pass as hostnames** (src/normalize.rs `host`) — **incorrectly closed in `2907b0d`, which only rejected a whole name starting with lowercase `0x`; `0x7f.0x1` and `x.0X7F000001` still loaded (reproduced in Audit 15). Now resolved in `943c586`: the final label is checked as this entry recommended. Tests: `hosts_ending_in_an_ipv4_number_are_rejected_in_configuration`, `normalizes_hosts_and_rejects_ambiguous_authorities`**
  - WHATWG URL parsing treats a host whose last label is `0x`-prefixed hex
    as IPv4: `0x7f000001` is `127.0.0.1`, and so is `0x7f.1`. Here
    `0x7f.1` is caught (last label `1`), but `0x7f000001` is not.
  - Probe: `host = "0x7f000001"` loads → `true`. The same request host
    would match that rule as if it were a DNS name.
  - Impact is limited: a config must name the IP-like host itself, and no
    domain-based rule matches it. Still, it contradicts the
    "unsupported IP literal" contract.
  - Resolve by extending the final-label check to WHATWG's "ends in a
    number": all digits, or `0x`/`0X` followed by hex digits (including a
    bare `0x`).

## Audit 9 — `7235e08` (2026-10-29)

Gates: `cargo fmt --check` OK · `cargo build` 0 warnings · `cargo test` 53/53
(the new `compiled_rules_only_retain_known_action_classes` runs) ·
`cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings` OK. Arch.md §8 was updated in the
same commit.

`CompiledRule.action_class` is now the `&'static str` from `ACTION_CLASSES`,
looked up in `CompiledRule::new`. `classify` can therefore only return a
predefined class, by construction (Arch.md §19). It also checks again what
`config.rs` validates, so the guard holds even if the two drift apart. No new
findings.

## Audit 10 — `db5a4c7`, `09a4754` (2026-10-29)

Gates (each from a clean export): `cargo fmt --check` OK · `cargo build`
0 warnings · `cargo test` 53/53 at both · `cargo clippy --all-targets -D
warnings` OK. Arch.md §17 now requires generated coverage to include valid,
matching requests, and `db5a4c7` provides it.

- [x] **LOW — Valid generated requests come from a fixed pool of 320 combinations** (tests/robustness.rs `generated_request`) — **resolved in `943c586`: `generated_equivalent_spellings_classify_identically` mutates valid tuples (host case, port, trailing dot, query, fragment, dot segments, escapes, trailing slash), and the method, host, and path generators produce varied valid values**
  - Valid tuples are picked from 4 methods × 4 hosts × 5 paths × 4 (the

    trailing dots and `//` never appear in a *valid* request.
  - So the trailing-slash comparison and host normalization are covered

## Audit 11 — `98788f4` (2026-10-29)

Gates (clean export): `cargo fmt --check` OK · `cargo build` 0 warnings ·
`cargo test` 58/58 (re-confirmed with an isolated build) · `cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings` OK. Arch.md §13,
§14, §16 and agents.md document the new limits in the same commit.

- [x] **MED — Plain exact-path rules use up the wildcard budget; about 400 ordinary rules fail to load** (src/matcher.rs `paths_overlap` → `globs_overlap`) — **resolved in `d2d8067`: literal pairs short-circuit, and the 400-rule probe now loads. See Audit 14 for the wildcard-prefix variant**
  - Any eligible pair whose paths differ goes through the product-NFA
    search, even when neither path contains `*`. Two same-length literals,
    such as `/api/00001` and `/api/00002`, have equal specificity, so each
    pair is charged `(len+1)²` states (121 here) just to learn that the
    paths differ.
  - Probe (clean export, release build): one set on `acme.com`, rules
    `path = "/api/NNNNN"` alternating `repo.read` / `repo.write`:

    | rules | result |
    |---|---|
    | 200 | loads (6 ms) |
    | 400 | `ConflictAnalysisTooComplex` ("rule 230 and rule 363") |
    | 800 / 2,000 / 10,000 | same error |

    That is an ordinary REST mapping, well under the documented 10,000-rule
    limit.
  - The new tests miss it: `same_class_rules_do_not_consume_overlap_budget`
    uses one class, so no pair is eligible. The error also blames a pair of
    rules that cannot conflict.
  - Resolve by spending budget only on wildcard-wildcard pairs:
    - neither path contains `*` → overlap is `left == right`;
    - exactly one contains `*` → overlap is
      `glob_matches(pattern, literal)`, which is linear in practice;
    - only two wildcard patterns need `globs_overlap`.

    Add a test with hundreds of different-class exact paths.

- [x] **LOW — Pattern-length cap is enforced only in `config.rs`** (`MAX_PATTERN_BYTES`) — **resolved in `2907b0d`: `CompiledRule::new` enforces `MAX_PATTERN_BYTES`**
  - `CompiledRule::new` accepts any length. The state-budget sizing assumes
    the cap, so any future path that builds rules without `config::parse`
    breaks that assumption. This is the same drift risk as the Audit 1
    subdomain item.
  - Move the check next to `normalize::pattern_path`, or into
    `CompiledRule::new`.

- [x] **LOW — Pairwise loop is O(n²) even when no budget is spent** — **closed as accepted (won't fix): within the 10,000-rule limit, and hardening.md rules out indexing beyond H6/H9**
  - 10,000 single-class exact rules took 136 ms to load in release (about
    50M pair comparisons), and debug builds are much slower. `load` runs in
    an HTTP handler (README).
  - This is acceptable for the stated limits. If larger configs matter,
    bucket rules by `(host pattern, specificity)` before comparing pairs.

## Audit 12 — `11bbeb6` (H7) … `fb3adea` (H11) (2026-10-29)

Gates (each commit from a clean export, re-run with an isolated `target/`
per commit after a shared build dir was found to give stale results): fmt OK ·
build 0 warnings · tests 59 / 60 / 61 / 61 / 61, all passing · clippy OK at
every commit. The probes below were re-confirmed with isolated builds. Each commit updates
Arch.md and agents.md together with the code.

- H7 rejects literal `;` in request and pattern paths. `%3B` is kept encoded.
  Tomcat, Jetty and Spring strip `;` parameters before decoding, so that is
  consistent.
- H8 ranks wildcard hosts by base depth (resolves the baseline item) and
  requires at least two labels in a base host.
- H9 caps methods at 32 bytes and raw paths at 8 KiB. That fails closed and
  matches common server request-line limits.
- H10 rejects `method = "*"` and configured dot segments, consistent with
  "explicit validation over silent correction".
- H11 includes the rejected value in `InvalidRule`. Arch.md §5/§14 now
  describe the real test layout and error enum, and the §14 example matches
  the actual `Display` output.

- [x] **MED (carried from Audit 11, still reproduces at `fb3adea`) — 400 exact-path rules with two classes fail with `ConflictAnalysisTooComplex`** — **resolved in `d2d8067`**
  - Same probe, same result ("rule 230 and rule 363"). None of H7–H11 touch
    `paths_overlap`.

- [ ] **LOW — Two-label minimum does not stop public-suffix bases; the new test relies on one** (src/config.rs `validate_host`, tests/classification.rs `deeper_wildcard_base_host_wins_before_path_specificity`)
  - `host = "co.uk"` with `subdomain = "*"` still loads.
  - Probe: `classify("POST", "api.bank.co.uk", "/transfer")` →
    `Some("llm.inference")`. Every `.co.uk` site gets whatever class the
    broad rule names. If policy allows that class, requests to unrelated
    sites are allowed.
  - Arch.md:332 presents the two-label rule as preventing wildcards rooted
    at a public suffix. It only covers single-label suffixes such as `com`.
  - Resolve with either:
    - (a) document it as a heuristic and say that multi-label public
      suffixes (`co.uk`, `com.au`, `github.io`) are the config author's
      responsibility, ideally with the test using a non-suffix base such as
      `example.co.uk`; or
    - (b) embed a small static denylist of common multi-label suffixes for
      `*` rules. The no-I/O constraint rules out fetching the PSL.

- [x] **LOW — Error messages echo the entire rejected value** (`SetError::InvalidRule { value }`, H11) — **resolved in `2907b0d` for `InvalidRule`/`UnknownActionClass` (256-byte `diagnostic_value`). See Audit 14 for TOML errors**
  - A 1 MB invalid `path` produces a 1,000,051-byte `LoadError` message.
    Callers often log or return this from an HTTP handler, so it can bloat
    logs or responses.
  - Truncate the stored or displayed value, e.g. to 128 characters plus
    `…`, and test it.

## Audit 13 — `5d78ae8` (H12) (2026-10-29)

Gates (clean export, isolated `target/`): fmt OK · build 0 warnings ·
`cargo test` 64/64 · clippy OK. Arch.md §9 (including a new "Known limits"
list) and agents.md were updated in the same commit.

Auditor process note: Audits 10–12 originally shared one `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`
across exports, and cargo reused stale artifacts. Pass/fail results still
hold after re-running each commit in isolation; only the test counts above
were corrected. Every audit from here on uses a fresh target per commit.

- [x] **MED — Rules with uppercase literals become unreachable when a broader rule covers their lowercase spelling** (src/lib.rs `classify`, H12) — **resolved in `649bdd7`/`2907b0d`: lowercased requests are compared with precomputed `folded_path`. The Twilio-style probe classifies as configured**
  - The lowercase alternative is matched against the original,
    case-sensitive patterns. A configured route such as
    `/2010-04-01/Accounts/*/Messages.json` (Twilio's real casing) matches
    the request as sent. But its lowercased copy `/2010-04-01/accounts/…`
    matches only a broader rule, so the classes "disagree".
  - Probe (Twilio-style set with a catch-all `/*` → `repo.read`):
    - `POST /2010-04-01/Accounts/AC123/Messages.json` → **`None`**.
      Expected `communication.external.send`. The broad
      `Accounts/*` rule with no method also loses.
    - The `GET` spellings return `repo.read` only because the catch-all
      happens to share that class.
  - This is the same nested-rule failure as Audit 4/6, now for any API
    whose paths contain capitals: Twilio, Azure, many AWS services. The new
    test `/v1/IDs/*` passes only because no broader rule exists.
  - Resolve by comparing case-insensitively on both sides. Precompute a
    lowercased copy of each pattern at load, and match the lowercased
    request against those copies for the alternative. A rule that matches
    as configured then also matches its own lowercase spelling, so only a
    genuinely different case-insensitive winner causes denial. Add a test
    with an uppercase-literal rule nested under a broader rule.

- [x] **LOW — `lowercase_path_outside_escapes` indexes without bounds checks** (src/normalize.rs, `bytes[index + 1]`, `bytes[index + 2]`) — **resolved in `2907b0d`: uses `bytes.get`**
  - Safe today, because callers pass only paths already validated by
    `decode_unreserved`. But this is a panic site on the `classify` path,
    and its safety rests on a cross-function invariant. agents.md: "No
    unwrap/expect on untrusted inputs; classify must never panic."
  - Use `bytes.get(index + 1..index + 3)` and copy whatever is present, or
    make it a private helper that takes the validated type.

- Still open at `5d78ae8`, re-confirmed with isolated builds: the Audit 11
  exact-path budget MED (400 rules → `ConflictAnalysisTooComplex`), the
  Audit 12 `co.uk` wildcard LOW, and the Audit 12 unbounded-error-value LOW
  (1 MB path → 1,000,051-byte message).

## Audit 14 — `649bdd7`, `d2d8067`, `2907b0d` (2026-10-29)

Gates (each commit, clean export, isolated `target/`): fmt OK · build
0 warnings · tests 63 / 64 / 67, all passing · clippy OK. Arch.md §7, §9,
§13, §14, §16 and agents.md updated in step.

Probes at `2907b0d`, release build:

| probe | result |
|---|---|
| 400 exact paths, 2 classes | **loads** (was `TooComplex`) |
| Twilio-style `POST …/Accounts/*/Messages.json` under `/*` | `communication.external.send` |
| same, lowercased | `None` (disagreement, as intended) |

- [ ] **MED — Wildcard rules with distinct literal prefixes still exhaust the budget** (src/matcher.rs `paths_overlap` → `globs_overlap`)
  - Probe: 400 rules `path = "/api/NNNNN/*"` alternating
    `repo.read`/`repo.write` → `ConflictAnalysisTooComplex` ("rule 212 and
    rule 307"). This is the most common REST mapping shape: `/v1/customers/*`,
    `/v1/charges/*`, `/v1/refunds/*` …, with different classes.
  - Two such patterns can never overlap, because their literal prefixes
    differ before the first `*`. Yet each pair is charged about
    `(len+1)²` states.
  - Resolve with a linear pre-check before `globs_overlap`:
    - compare the literal prefixes up to each pattern's first `*`, and the
      literal suffixes after each pattern's last `*`;
    - if either pair diverges within the shorter length, return
      `Ok(false)` without spending budget.

    Add the 400-rule prefix-wildcard case as a test.

- [ ] **LOW — `rust-version = "1.85"` is too low** (Cargo.toml)
  - `src/config.rs` uses `if let … &&` let-chains (e.g. lines 60–61 and
    69–71), which were stabilised in Rust **1.88**. Edition 2024 alone
    allows them only from 1.88.
  - On 1.85–1.87, Cargo accepts the declared MSRV and rustc then fails on
    the let-chains. That is the confusing failure the field is meant to
    prevent. Changing `is_multiple_of` to `% 5 == 0` in `robustness.rs` does
    not help.
  - Set `rust-version = "1.88"`. Only 1.95 and stable are installed here, so
    this was not verified by building on 1.85.

- [ ] **LOW — TOML parse errors are still unbounded** (`SetError::Toml`)
  - `toml`'s error display quotes the offending source line. Probe: an
    invalid document with a 1 MB line gives a **2,000,160-byte** `LoadError`
    message.
  - `diagnostic_value` covers only `InvalidRule` and `UnknownActionClass`.
    Store a bounded rendering, such as the message without the snippet or
    a truncated `to_string()`, or cap the input size before parsing.

- Still open: the `co.uk` public-suffix wildcard LOW from Audit 12. It still
  loads at `2907b0d`.

## Audit 15 — final security and submission pass (2026-10-31)

Base `2907b0d`; the fixes below were committed together as `943c586`.

Gates (fresh `target/`): `cargo fmt --check` OK · `cargo build` 0 warnings ·
`cargo test --all-targets` 83/83 (67 at the base) ·
`cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` OK. Each fix below had a failing
test first: 7 tests failed against `2907b0d`.

Rechecked at the base and already fixed, with no code change needed:

- `POST /v1//refunds/x` returns `None`; `//` in a pattern fails to load.
- `remove_dot_segments` is linear. At the 8 KiB cap, `classify` took 20–62 µs
  per call in release for the worst dot-heavy paths. The new guard fails when
  the old buffer-shifting algorithm is put back.

- [x] **HIGH — Method folding could report a less sensitive class than a case-sensitive server executes** (`src/lib.rs` `classify`) — **resolved in `943c586`**
  - Rules `/x` → `payment.refund` and `GET /x` → `payment.read`: `get /x`
    returned `payment.read`. A case-sensitive router (Go's `ServeMux`) sends
    `get` to the catch-all handler, so the refund runs classified as a read.
  - A folded and a case-sensitive reading are now compared, and disagreement
    returns `None`. This changes one existing expectation:
    `method_case_does_not_fall_through_to_method_less_rule` now asserts `None`
    instead of `payment.refund` for `delete`/`Delete`. Action classes have no
    sensitivity order, so the two directions cannot be told apart.
  - Tests: `method_case_cannot_reach_a_less_sensitive_method_specific_rule`,
    `method_case_classifies_when_both_readings_agree`,
    `generated_method_case_never_selects_a_class_one_reading_contradicts`.

- [x] **HIGH — Classification depended on rule order for patterns differing only by case** (`src/lib.rs` `best_match`) — **resolved in `943c586`**
  - Rules `/v1/Refunds` → `payment.refund` and `/v1/refunds` → `payment.read`
    pass the load check but tie once folded, and `max_by` picked the last.
    `/v1/Refunds` returned `None` in one order and `payment.refund` in the other,
    against README "no precedence". A tie now denies the request.
  - Tests: `patterns_differing_only_by_case_do_not_depend_on_rule_order`,
    `generated_rule_sets_classify_identically_in_every_order`.

- [x] **LOW — `classify` is slow at the configuration limits with adversarial patterns** (`glob_matches`, new in this audit) — **closed as documented (won't fix): needs hostile mapping files, recorded in Arch.md §16; hardening.md rules out further performance work**
  - 10,000 rules of about 1 KiB `/*a*a…b` against an 8 KiB `/`-ending path took
    0.64 s (`GET`) and 1.29 s (`get`) in release, compared with 0.4 ms for 10,000
    ordinary exact rules. It needs such patterns in the mapping files, so it
    is not reachable from requests alone. Documented in Arch.md §16.

- Rechecked and still open at this audit: Audit 14 MED (400 `/api/NNNNN/*` rules →
  `ConflictAnalysisTooComplex`; 200 load), Audit 14 LOW `rust-version`, Audit 14
  LOW TOML errors (1 MB line → 2,000,134-byte message), Audit 12 LOW `co.uk`
  (still loads), Audit 11 LOW pair loop (10,000 rules, 138 ms), Baseline LOW per-call
  allocations.

## Baseline gaps (pre-existing, found during Audit 1)

- [x] **MED — No generated-input robustness tests** (Arch.md §17 "Robustness — **started in `c2e2283` and `db5a4c7`; resolved in `943c586`: `tests/robustness.rs` now has generated malformed-method, host, and path checks, a reference wildcard matcher, and rule-order, method-case, and equivalent-spelling properties**
  tests", agents.md completion gates)
  - Coverage is hand-picked inputs only. Arch asks for property-based or
    fuzz-style tests that `classify` never panics, is deterministic, and is
    unaffected by rule order.
  - A dev-only `proptest` (or a seeded byte-generator loop with no new
    dependency) would satisfy it.

- [x] **LOW — Wildcard hosts with different base depths tie on host specificity** (src/matcher.rs `specificity`) — **resolved in `f04706c`: base-host label depth ranks right after host kind**
  - `*` on `acme.com` and `*` on `api.acme.com` both score `host = 0`. For
    `x.api.acme.com`, the deeper base doesn't rank higher, so path/method
    decide, and an equal-specificity tie becomes a load-time conflict.
  - This is deterministic and safe, but probably surprising. Consider adding
    base-host label count to host specificity, and document the result in
    Arch.md §11.

- [x] **LOW — Compiled rules store `action_class: String`** (Arch.md §8 suggests `&'static str`) — **resolved in `7235e08`**
  - Store the matching `ACTION_CLASSES` entry instead. This also makes "only
    predefined classes can be returned" hold by construction rather than by
    validation order.

- [x] **LOW — `classify` allocates per call** — **closed as won't fix: no benchmark shows it matters (Arch.md §15)** (method `String`, host
  `String`, path `String`, plus the stripped-slash re-scan)
  - Fine at the expected scale (Arch.md §15 allows a linear scan). Revisit
    only if benchmarks show it matters.

1	AGENTS.md — Firma HTTP Action Classifier
2	Mission and source of truth
3	Build the Rust library described in README.md: parse TOML mapping sets and classify (method, host, path) into one of the existing ACTION_CLASSES, or None. This is a library, not an HTTP proxy, agent harness, policy engine, UI, network service, or LLM. Never add I/O, networking, databases, or a CLI.
4	
5	Read README.md, Cargo.toml, src/lib.rs, and tests/example.rs before editing. The project design document describes our chosen implementation policies; the repository README and the fixed API take precedence if there is any disagreement. Record and surface ambiguities rather than inventing undocumented API behavior.
6	
7	Public API signatures are fixed:
8	pub async fn load(sets: &[&str]) -> Result<Classifier, LoadError>;
9	impl Classifier {
10	    pub async fn classify(&self, method: &str, host: &str, path: &str) -> Option<&str>;
11	}
12	Keep ACTION_CLASSES unchanged. Keep all four supplied example tests passing. LoadError can be redesigned but must implement std::error::Error. No unwrap/expect on untrusted inputs; classify must never panic. The classifier must be immutable after load, Send + Sync, and fast to query.
13	Workflow: two parallel owners, one integrator, one reviewer
14	Use two concurrent implementation agents. A third agent (Integrator) works after both are ready; an optional fourth (Security Reviewer) inspects the merged result without simultaneously editing it. Do not run multiple agents with write access to the same worktree.
15	
16	Prefer separate Git worktrees and branches:
17	# Run from the repository root; example names only.
18	git worktree add ../firma-config -b agent/config
19	git worktree add ../firma-matcher -b agent/matcher
20	Agent 1 — Configuration, validation, and compilation input
21	Owns: src/config.rs and configuration-focused tests (tests/config_validation.rs or module-local tests). Can propose—but not unilaterally edit—shared public types or src/lib.rs.
22	
23	Responsibilities:
24	- Deserialize mapping sets and rules with Serde; #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)] on both.
25	- Validate format version (1), required/nonempty fields, allowed action classes, host/subdomain/method/path syntax, and empty rules as defined in the design.
26	- Parse all provided TOML strings, with no filesystem reads; collect source identifiers (input set index, optional name, rule index).
27	- Expose validated configuration records for Agent 2's compiler/matcher representation.
28	- Design structured load errors, including cross-set conflict diagnostics; coordinate error implementation with the Integrator.
29	- Ensure set order never establishes precedence.
30	- Do not create a separate host/path matcher or overlap algorithm in config.rs.
31	Deliver: exported types/functions and tests; notes for Integrator documenting validation invariants, error metadata, and unresolved interface needs.
32	Agent 2 — HTTP normalization, matching, and overlap primitives
33	Owns: src/normalize.rs, src/matcher.rs, and their focused tests. Do not edit src/config.rs; avoid modifying src/lib.rs or Cargo.toml without agreeing on an integration interface.
34	
35	Responsibilities:
36	- Implement safe request normalization (host, method, path) and reject malformed/ambiguous requests with no panic.
37	- Implement compiled exact/wildcard host, method, and path matching.
38	- Define deterministic, documented specificity ordering independent of set order.
39	- Provide rule-overlap detection using the same semantics as runtime matching. Overlap must account for valid normalized request inputs, not just string equality.
40	- Expose a stable interface for validated rules and/or compilation; do not parse TOML.
41	- Write specificity, wildcard, Unicode, adversarial input, and property/fuzz-style tests where practical.
42	Deliver: exported types/functions and tests; notes for Integrator documenting matching semantics, overlap guarantees, and unsupported inputs.
43	Integrator — after both implementation branches land
44	Owns: src/lib.rs, integration adjustments to shared types, Cargo.toml if required, and cross-module tests (tests/classification.rs, tests/conflicts.rs, tests/security.rs). One integration owner only.
45	
46	Responsibilities:
47	- Reconcile module interfaces (do not maintain duplicate canonicalization or matching logic).
48	- Implement the fixed load() function: parse -> validate -> compile -> detect conflicts -> return immutable classifier.
49	- Implement the fixed classify() function: normalize -> find matching compiled rules -> select highest specificity -> return static class or None.
50	- Use source locations from config to generate actionable LoadError variants.
51	- Reject equal-specificity overlapping rules with different classes; allow same-class duplicates and overlaps where one rule has greater specificity. Be conservative when exact overlap cannot be proved: reject unsupported/ambiguous patterns rather than silently accept potential conflicts.
52	- Ensure the same canonicalization contract is applied to rule literals and request inputs.
53	- Run all tests and verify Send + Sync, deterministic set-order behavior, and no warnings.
54	Security Reviewer — after integration (read-only first)
55	Independently review the completed implementation for bypasses, specificity ambiguities, normalization differences between load and classify, panic paths, excessive allocations, unsupported upstream HTTP semantics, and configuration conflicts. Produce reproducible failing tests or concrete findings before requesting targeted fixes. Do not rewrite the architecture without a demonstrated defect.
56	Shared behavior contract

# Take-home: action classifier

**Time budget: at most 2 hours of human time.** We expect you to use a coding
agent, and we are as interested in the process as in the result.

## Context

An AI agent's outbound HTTP requests are classified into *action classes*
(`payment.refund`, `repo.write`, ...). Policies then allow or deny action
classes instead of naming every provider. The classification is driven by
**mapping sets**: TOML files that say "requests to this host, method and path
are action class X". The caller denies any request the classifier does not
classify, so a wrong answer here is a security bug, not a cosmetic one.

You will build the classification core as a library. No I/O, network,
database or CLI.

## What to build

Implement the two functions in `src/lib.rs`. Their signatures are fixed;
everything else is yours to design.

```rust
pub async fn load(sets: &[&str]) -> Result<Classifier, LoadError>;
impl Classifier { pub async fn classify(&self, method: &str, host: &str, path: &str) -> Option<&str>; }
```

`load` takes the text of one or more user-provided mapping files. `classify`
returns the action class for a request, or `None` when it is unclassified.

## Mapping file format

```toml
format_version = 1
name = "Acme Payments"
description = "Acme payments API mappings"
host = "acme.com"

[[rules]]
method = "GET"
subdomain = "api"
path = "/v1/payment_intents"
action_class = "payment.read"

[[rules]]
subdomain = "api"
path = "/v1/refunds/*"
action_class = "payment.refund"

[[rules]]
path = "/pricing"
action_class = "payment.read"
```

- A rule applies to the host formed by its `subdomain` followed by the file's
  `host`. With `host = "acme.com"`:
  - `subdomain = "api"` applies to `api.acme.com`;
  - `subdomain = "*"` applies to any subdomain of `acme.com`, such as
    `a.acme.com`;
  - no `subdomain` applies to `acme.com` itself.
- `subdomain`, `method` and `path` are optional. Omitting `method` or `path`
  matches everything.
- `*` in a path is a wildcard.
- `action_class` must be one of `ACTION_CLASSES` in `src/lib.rs`.
- Unknown keys are an error, so misspelled keys fail loudly.

## Behavior

- Both functions will be called from inside an HTTP handler.
- When several rules match a request, **the most specific wins**.
- Sets are loaded together, with no precedence.
- Requests are matched as an HTTP client would send them.
- `classify` must never panic.

## Deliverables

1. The crate, building with no warnings and with `cargo test` passing.
2. Your complete AI session transcript, in the most detailed form your tool
   offers. Do not summarise, redact or `--sanitize` it. We want to see the
   instructions, skills, files and documents you gave the agent, as well as
   its tool calls. Send the raw session file, plus the readable export if
   your tool has one:
   - **Claude Code:** the raw file
     `~/.claude/projects/<project>/<session-id>.jsonl` (`<project>` is your
     working directory path with every non-alphanumeric character replaced by
     `-`; sessions older than 30 days are deleted by default), and
     optionally `/export session.txt`.
   - **Codex:** the raw file
     `~/.codex/sessions/<year>/<month>/<day>/rollout-*.jsonl`, and
     optionally `/export session.md`.
   - **opencode:** `opencode export <sessionID> > session.json` (run
     `opencode export` without an ID to pick the session; do not pass
     `--sanitize`).
   - If you used several sessions, send all of them. Also send any
     instruction files, skills or notes you wrote or installed for the agent
     (for example `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, or a `SKILL.md`).

We will read your code, your tests and your transcript, then spend about 45
minutes discussing them with you.

1	# HARDENING.md — steering for the coding agent
2	
3	Read this after `README.md`, `agents.md` and `Arch.md`. It turns the security
4	audit of `b2d8402` (see `backlog.md`) into ordered, bounded work items.
5	
6	Precedence stays the same: README > fixed API > `agents.md` > `Arch.md` > this
7	file. If an item here conflicts with the README, stop and flag it.
8	
9	## Ground rules
10	
11	1. **Follow the design; only extend it where a defect was demonstrated.** Every
12	   item below either brings the code back in line with `Arch.md` (Tier 1), or
13	   adds to the design to close a reproduced problem (Tier 2/3). Do not
14	   restructure modules, add indexing, add dependencies, or "optimize" beyond
15	   what an item asks for. A linear scan is the accepted design (Arch §15).
16	2. **One item per commit.** Each commit contains the code change, a test that
17	   would have failed before it, and the matching `Arch.md` / `agents.md` edit.
18	   Code and docs must never disagree at any commit. The commit message names
19	   the item number (e.g. `H6: total conflict-analysis budget`).
20	3. **Never weaken a test to make it pass.** Never write a test that asserts the
21	   *less* sensitive class for an alternate spelling of a request. If a test
22	   seems wrong, stop and report rather than editing the expectation.
23	4. **Fail closed.** When unsure, the request is unclassified (`None`) or the
24	   config is rejected with an explicit `LoadError`. Never pick a class by
25	   guessing.
26	5. **Don't flip-flop on policy.** The policies in `Arch.md` §7/§9/§11 are
27	   decided. Do not revert method folding, `//` rejection, multi-label
28	   subdomains, or linear dot-segment removal.
29	6. **Same canonicalization both sides.** Any new path or host rule goes in the
30	   shared helpers in `normalize.rs` and applies to both config patterns and
31	   requests, unless the item says otherwise.
32	7. **Gates on every commit**, run from `Firma_take_home/`:
33	   ```bash
34	   cargo fmt --all -- --check
35	   cargo build
36	   cargo test
37	   cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings
38	   ```
39	   The four tests in `tests/example.rs` must pass unchanged.
40	8. No `unwrap`/`expect` on untrusted input. `classify` must never panic. Keep
41	   `Classifier` `Send + Sync` and immutable after `load`.
42	
43	## Work order
44	
45	Do the items in this order. Stop after each tier and report.
46	
47	---
48	
49	## Tier 1 — make the code match the design
50	
51	### H1. Check trailing slashes in one direction only (open HIGH, Audit 4/6)
52	
53	- **Problem:** `classify` also checks `/x` against `/x/`. A narrower rule under
54	  a broader wildcard can never match: with `/v1/*/send` →
55	  `communication.external.send` and `/v1/*` → `payment.read`,
56	  `GET api.acme.com/v1/msg/send` returns `None`. This breaks README "the most
57	  specific wins".
58	- **Change (`src/lib.rs` `classify`):** only when the normalized path ends in
59	  `/` and isn't `/`, classify the path without that slash as well. Return
60	  `None` only if that result is `Some` and differs. A path without a trailing
61	  slash gets no alternate check.
62	- **Rationale for the doc:** the risk is a server stripping a trailing slash
63	  and running a more sensitive handler than the one classified. A request sent
64	  without the slash is already classified as sent.
65	- **Tests:**
66	  - `tests/classification.rs` `most_specific_rule_wins`: `/v1/msg/send` →
67	    `Some("communication.external.send")`.
68	  - `tests/security.rs`: `POST /v1/payouts` → `Some("payment.create")`, and
69	    `POST /v1/payouts/` → `None`.
70	  - Rename the security test to match the one-directional behaviour.
71	- **Docs:** Arch §9 and agents.md "Paths" say the check goes one way, with the
72	  rationale above.
73	
74	### H2. Reject IP-like hosts (Arch §7, §9)
75	
76	- **Problem:** only dotted-quad IPv4 is rejected. `010.0.0.1` and `127.1` load
77	  as config hosts and are accepted as request hosts.
78	- **Change (`normalize::host`):** reject any host whose last label is all
79	  digits. No real TLD is all-numeric (RFC 3696 §2). Config uses the same
80	  helper, so both sides are covered.
81	- **Tests:** a config `host` of `127.1` or `010.0.0.1` is rejected. A request
82	  host of `127.1`, `010.0.0.1` or `1.2.3.4.5` gives `None`.
83	
84	### H3. Store the action class as `&'static str` (Arch §8)
85	
86	- **Change:** `CompiledRule::action_class` holds the matching `ACTION_CLASSES`
87	  entry, found at compile time. An unknown class is a `CompileError`, which
88	  `load` maps to `SetError::UnknownActionClass`. `best_match` returns the
89	  stored reference.
90	- **Why:** only the seven classes can come back, guaranteed by the type rather
91	  than by validation order.
92	
93	### H4. Make the robustness tests reach the matcher (Arch §17)
94	
95	- **Problem:** the generator's alphabet doesn't contain `c`, `m` or `e`, so no
96	  generated host is ever under `acme.com`. Both tests only ever compare `None`
97	  with `None`.
98	- **Change (`tests/robustness.rs`):**
99	  - Pick the method from {`GET`, `POST`, `DELETE`, `get`, generated junk}.
100	  - Pick the host from {`api.acme.com`, `x.acme.com`, `a.b.acme.com`,
101	    `acme.com`, generated junk}.
102	  - Build the path from valid segments (`v1`, `refunds`, `x`, `.`, `..`,
103	    `%72efunds`, an empty last segment), then randomly mutate one byte.
104	- **Asserts:**
105	  - Results are deterministic and independent of set order.
106	  - Every result is `None` or a member of `ACTION_CLASSES`.
107	  - At least 25% of iterations classify to `Some`, so the test fails if the
108	    generator stops reaching the matcher again.
109	  - Use no new dependencies.
110	
111	### H5. Test cleanups
112	
113	- `tests/conflicts.rs` `same_class_duplicates_are_harmless`: change the path
114	  back from `/x*` to `/x`.
115	- `tests/security.rs` `method_case_does_not_fall_through_to_method_less_rule`:
116	  remove the standalone `DELETE` assertion that the loop already covers.
117	- `tests/conflicts.rs:165`: remove the stale "Exact subdomains are one DNS
118	  label" comment.
119	
120	---
121	
122	## Tier 2 — hardening that adds to the design
123	
124	### H6. Bound the cost of conflict analysis by total work, not pair count (MED)
125	
126	- **Problem:**
127	  - The 1M-state cap per pair multiplies across up to 100k pairs. 40 wildcard
128	    rules (a 42 KB config) take 21.6 s to load in release.
129	  - The pair cap counts *every* pair, so 448 rules on unrelated hosts fail with
130	    a misleading `ConflictAnalysisTooComplex` that names unrelated rules.
131	- **Change (`src/matcher.rs`, `src/config.rs`):**
132	  1. **Pattern length limit:** reject config `path` patterns longer than
133	     1024 bytes after normalization (`SetError::InvalidRule`, field `path`).
134	  2. **Total budget:** replace `MAX_CONFLICT_PAIR_CHECKS` with one total
135	     budget of glob-overlap states for the whole load (e.g. 4,000,000).
136	     Charge it only for pairs that reach `globs_overlap`, i.e. different
137	     class, equal specificity, and overlapping method and host. Cheap pairs
138	     cost nothing.
139	  3. **Short-circuit identical patterns:** before any budget check, two equal
140	     patterns (or both `None`) count as overlapping, so identical rules report
141	     `ConflictingRules`, not "too complex".
142	  4. **Rule-count limit:** add an explicit limit on total rules (e.g. 10,000)
143	     with its own `LoadError` variant, so the n² pair loop stays bounded.
144	- **Tests:**
145	  - 1,000 rules on 1,000 different hosts load.
146	  - 600 same-class exact paths in one set load.
147	  - The 40-rule adversarial config is rejected (too complex) or loads in under
148	    1 s in a debug build.
149	  - Two identical 1,000-`*` patterns with different classes give
150	    `ConflictingRules`.
151	  - A 1,025-byte pattern is rejected.
152	- **Docs:** Arch §13, §14 (list every `LoadError` variant) and §16 (state the
153	  limits and why).
154	
155	### H7. Leave paths containing `;` unclassified (HIGH)
156	
157	- **Problem:** `POST /v1/refunds;jsessionid=x/re_1` gives `payment.read`.
158	  Tomcat, Jetty and Spring strip `;` path parameters and run the refund.
159	- **Change:** reject a literal `;` in `normalize_path`, which covers both
160	  requests and patterns. `%3B` stays an encoded literal and is still accepted.
161	- **Tests (`tests/security.rs`):** `/v1/refunds;x/re_1` and
162	  `/v1/refunds;/re_1` give `None`. A config pattern containing `;` is
163	  rejected.
164	- **Docs:** add `;` to the rejected-forms list in Arch §7/§9 and agents.md
165	  "Paths", with the reason (servers strip path parameters).
166	
167	### H8. Wildcard host rules: deeper base wins; no single-label base hosts (MED)
168	
169	- **Problem:** a set with `host = "com"`, `subdomain = "*"`, `path = "/v1/*"`
170	  → `llm.inference` overrides Stripe's `*` rule on `stripe.com`.
171	  `POST api.stripe.com/v1/refunds/x` gives `llm.inference`, which breaks
172	  README "no precedence".
173	- **Change:**
174	  1. **Ranking:** in `Specificity`, put host *kind* (exact/bare beats wildcard)
175	     first, then base-host label count, before any path field. Exact and bare
176	     hosts use their full label count; they only overlap when the host strings
177	     are equal, so it doesn't change their ordering.
178	  2. **Config check:** reject a config `host` with fewer than two labels
179	     (`InvalidField("host")`).
180	- **Tests:**
181	  - With the Stripe set and a `co.uk`-style broad set loaded together,
182	    Stripe's rule wins for `api.stripe.com`.
183	  - `host = "com"` is rejected.
184	  - The existing tests that two wildcard rules on bases at the same depth
185	    conflict still pass.
186	- **Docs:** Arch §11 and agents.md "Specificity" add base depth after host
187	  kind. Arch §7 says the base host needs at least two labels.
188	
189	### H9. Cap input sizes (LOW)
190	
191	- **Change:**
192	  - A request `path` input longer than 8 KiB, measured before stripping the
193	    query, gives `None`.
194	  - A method longer than 32 bytes gives `None`.
195	  - Hosts are already bounded by the DNS length check.
196	- **Tests:** an 8,193-byte path gives `None`. An 8,192-byte valid path still
197	  classifies.
198	- **Docs:** Arch §9 and §16.
199	
200	### H10. Reject confusing config values (LOW)
201	
202	- `method = "*"` gives `InvalidRule { field: "method" }`. Someone might read it
203	  as "any method"; omitting `method` is how to say that.
204	- A config path with a `.` or `..` segment is rejected, whether or not it
205	  contains a wildcard. Today `/v1/../admin` is silently rewritten to `/admin`,
206	  which Arch §7 forbids ("no silent correction").
207	- Docs: Arch §7.
208	
209	### H11. Error detail and doc sync (LOW)
210	
211	- Add the rejected value to `SetError::InvalidRule` (e.g.
212	  `value: String`, Debug-quoted in the message).
213	- Arch §14:
214	  - List every variant that exists, including `ConflictAnalysisTooComplex` and
215	    the new limits.
216	  - Say that set and rule indexes are 0-based, and make the example messages
217	    match the real `Display` output.
218	- Arch §5: list `tests/robustness.rs`, and say config tests live in
219	  `src/config.rs` rather than `tests/config_validation.rs`.
220	
221	---
222	
223	## Tier 3 — judgement call (owner decides; default below)
224	
225	### H12. Uppercase path spellings (HIGH, behaviour depends on the server)
226	
227	- **Problem:** `POST /v1/REFUNDS/re_1` gives `payment.read`. Express and
228	  ASP.NET Core route case-insensitively by default.
229	- **Default: (b), if time allows; otherwise (a).**
230	  - **(a) Document only:** add "case-insensitive server routing" to the
231	    known-limits list in Arch §9.
232	  - **(b) Disagreement check:**
233	    - Also classify the path with ASCII letters lowercased *outside*
234	      percent escapes, so `%3A` stays `%3A`.
235	    - If that result is `Some` and differs from the original, return `None`.
236	    - Combine this with H1: check every alternate spelling (lowercased,
237	      stripped trailing slash, both). Deny if any alternate that isn't `None`
238	      disagrees.
239	    - Don't lowercase the path itself or the rules; IDs can be case-sensitive.
240	    - Document in §9 that this only catches rules written in lowercase, which
241	      is the usual convention.
242	
243	### Document only, no code
244	
245	Add these to a "Known limits" list in Arch §9:
246	
247	- Trailing dots or `%20` at the end of a segment (IIS and others trim them).
248	- Method-override headers (`X-HTTP-Method-Override`): the classifier never
249	  sees headers.
250	- Servers that decode a path twice (`%252e`).
251	- Request bodies, and any routing that depends on the provider.
252	
253	---
254	
255	## Out of scope — do not do
256	
257	- No new action classes, public API changes, I/O, CLI, or dependencies.
258	- No rule indexing, caching, tries or other performance changes beyond H6/H9.
259	- No change to the method-folding, `//`, multi-label subdomain or dot-segment
260	  policies.
261	- Do not edit `backlog.md` entries other than marking items `[x]` with the
262	  fixing commit.
263	
264	## Report after each tier
265	
266	For each item:
267	- the commit hash;
268	- the files changed;
269	- the tests added (name and what they prove);
270	- the gate results, with exact counts (`cargo test N/N`);
271	- the doc sections edited;
272	- anything you were unsure about or deliberately left undone.
273	
274	Do not claim a tier is done if any gate fails.
275

1	# Audit backlog
2	
3	Findings from auditing each change against `README.md` (authoritative), `Arch.md`
4	and `agents.md`. The auditor only records findings; it does not change code.
5	Each entry: severity, the commit it was found in, the evidence, and a suggested
6	resolution. Mark resolved entries `[x]` with the fixing commit.
7	
8	Severity: **HIGH** = classification/security impact or spec violation,
9	**MED** = code/doc drift or missing required coverage, **LOW** = hardening.
10	
11	---
12	
13	## Audit 1 — `e8d5871`, `04ce80a` (2026-10-29)
14	
15	Gates: `cargo fmt --check` OK · `cargo build` 0 warnings · `cargo test` 46/46 ·
16	`cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings` OK.
17	
18	- [x] **HIGH — Method case-folding reverted; the fall-through bypass is back and is now asserted as expected behaviour** (`04ce80a`) — **resolved in `fc32096`: folding restored. Superseded by Audit 15, because folding alone left the reverse case open; non-uppercase spellings that disagree now return `None`**
19	  - `normalize::method` (src/normalize.rs:31) no longer upper-cases. With the
20	    rules in `tests/security.rs`, `classify("delete", "api.acme.com",
21	    "/v1/charges/ch_1")` returns `payment.read`. `DELETE` returns
22	    `payment.refund`. `method_matching_is_case_sensitive` now asserts
23	    `payment.read` for `delete`/`Delete`.
24	  - That contradicts the module doc at the top of `tests/security.rs`
25	    ("must not reach a broader, less sensitive rule"). It also contradicts
26	    `Arch.md:340`, `Arch.md:426`, `Arch.md:464` and `agents.md:61`, which all
27	    say methods are folded to uppercase.
28	  - Resolve by picking one policy and making code, tests and both docs agree:
29	    - (a) Restore folding.
30	    - (b) Keep case-sensitivity, revert the doc lines, and close the
31	      fall-through another way. For example, return `None` when the method
32	      is not all uppercase and a method-specific rule would have matched
33	      its uppercased form. Or reject non-uppercase methods outright.
34	
35	    Either way, a test should not assert that `delete` gets the less sensitive
36	    class.
37	
38	- [x] **MED — Single-label subdomain restriction contradicts the docs** (`e8d5871`) — **resolved in `8a43772`: multi-label subdomains allowed again, matching `Arch.md:333`**
39	  - `config.rs` now rejects `subdomain = "api.eu"` (`is_dns_label`).
40	    `Arch.md:333` says "`*` or one or more valid DNS labels" and cites the
41	    README.
42	  - This is fail-closed, so there's no security impact. It's a deliberate
43	    narrowing of the README's "subdomain followed by host" wording.
44	  - Resolve by updating `Arch.md:333` back to a single label with a one-line
45	    rationale (the same host can still be written as `host = "eu.acme.com"`,
46	    `subdomain = "api"`), or by reverting the restriction.
47	
48	- [x] **LOW — `CompiledRule::new` still accepts dotted subdomains** (src/matcher.rs, `Some(value) => normalize::host(value)`) — **resolved in `8a43772`: config and matcher both accept DNS names again**
49	  - Only `config.rs` enforces the one-label rule. `agents.md` asks for one
50	    canonicalization contract, not checks duplicated per module. If anything
51	    builds a `CompiledRule` without going through `config::parse`, the two
52	    disagree.
53	  - Resolve by enforcing the label rule in the shared helper, or by having
54	    `CompiledRule::new` take an already-validated subdomain.
55	
56	## Audit 2 — `80ff741` (2026-10-29)
57	
58	Gates: `cargo fmt --check` OK · `cargo build` 0 warnings · `cargo test` 46/46 ·
59	`cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings` OK.
60	
61	- [x] **HIGH — `//` paths accepted again; the fall-through bypass is now asserted as expected** (`80ff741`) — **resolved in `fc32096` via option (a): `//` rejected. Re-verified in Audit 15: `empty_path_segments_are_unclassified` and `generated_paths_classify_only_when_they_are_unambiguous`**
62	  - `classify("POST", "api.acme.com", "/v1//refunds/x")` returns
63	    `payment.read`, but `/v1/refunds/x` returns `payment.refund`.
64	    `duplicate_path_segments_are_preserved_for_matching` asserts the
65	    `payment.read` result.
66	  - Servers that merge slashes (nginx `merge_slashes on` by default, many
67	    framework routers) execute the refund. The agent gets a refund
68	    classified as a read.
69	  - It contradicts `Arch.md:351`, `Arch.md:436`, `agents.md:63` and the
70	    `tests/security.rs` module doc. The README says "Requests are matched as
71	    an HTTP client would send them", and the server-side interpretation is
72	    what makes the action dangerous.
73	  - Resolve by picking a policy and syncing code, tests and docs:
74	    - (a) Restore rejection, i.e. return `None`. That is fail-closed, and
75	      real clients essentially never send `//`.
76	    - (b) Collapse `//` for both rules and requests.
77	    - (c) Keep preserving it, but apply the same disagreement check
78	      already used for trailing slashes: classify the collapsed spelling too
79	      and return `None` if the classes differ.
80	
81	    Do not keep a test that asserts the less sensitive class.
82	
83	- [x] **MED — Quadratic `remove_dot_segments` reintroduced** (src/normalize.rs, `80ff741`) — **resolved in `fc32096`: linear stack version restored. Re-verified in Audit 15: `normalization_stays_linear_well_beyond_the_request_limit`**
84	  - The `String::drain(..n)` / `replace_range` loop shifts the remaining
85	    buffer once per segment, so cost is O(segments × length).
86	  - With the same algorithm at `0ea6f30`, a 64 KB path took about 21 ms
87	    per `classify` in release, and much longer in debug.
88	  - That path is attacker-controlled input to an HTTP handler. The linear
89	    stack version this replaced can keep empty segments: push `""`
90	    segments instead of rejecting them.
91	  - At minimum, cap the request path length (e.g. 8 KiB, then `None`) and
92	    test it.
93	
94	- [x] **LOW — `//` in patterns is accepted silently** (`pattern_path("/v1//x")`) — **resolved in `fc32096`: `pattern_path("/v1//x")` is `None`. Re-verified in Audit 15: `configured_patterns_follow_the_request_path_rules`**
95	  - Under the current policy a rule `/v1//x` is legal and distinct from
96	    `/v1/x`. Whatever HIGH resolution is chosen, patterns should follow the
97	    same rule as requests: rejected or collapsed in both, not one of each.
98	
99	## Audit 3 — `8a43772`, `fc32096` (2026-10-29)
100	
101	Gates: `cargo fmt --check` OK · `cargo build` 0 warnings · `cargo test` 47/47 ·
102	`cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings` OK.
103	
104	These commits restore the documented policies (multi-label subdomains,
105	upper-case method folding, `//` rejection, linear dot-segment removal). Code,
106	tests, `Arch.md` and `agents.md` agree again on all Audit 1/2 items.
107	
108	- [x] **LOW — Redundant assertion in `method_case_does_not_fall_through_to_method_less_rule`** (tests/security.rs) — **resolved in `09a4754`**
109	  - The standalone `DELETE` assertion duplicates the first iteration of the

48	- Implement the fixed load() function: parse -> validate -> compile -> detect conflicts -> return immutable classifier.
49	- Implement the fixed classify() function: normalize -> find matching compiled rules -> select highest specificity -> return static class or None.
50	- Use source locations from config to generate actionable LoadError variants.
51	- Reject equal-specificity overlapping rules with different classes; allow same-class duplicates and overlaps where one rule has greater specificity. Be conservative when exact overlap cannot be proved: reject unsupported/ambiguous patterns rather than silently accept potential conflicts.
52	- Ensure the same canonicalization contract is applied to rule literals and request inputs.
53	- Run all tests and verify Send + Sync, deterministic set-order behavior, and no warnings.
54	Security Reviewer — after integration (read-only first)
55	Independently review the completed implementation for bypasses, specificity ambiguities, normalization differences between load and classify, panic paths, excessive allocations, unsupported upstream HTTP semantics, and configuration conflicts. Produce reproducible failing tests or concrete findings before requesting targeted fixes. Do not rewrite the architecture without a demonstrated defect.
56	Shared behavior contract
57	These are chosen policies from the technical design, not all explicit README requirements. If a policy conflicts with a direct README requirement, follow README and flag the difference.
58	
59	Hosts: Case-insensitive ASCII DNS hostnames; lower-case for comparison. Request host may have a valid numeric port and one trailing DNS dot; reject empty labels, malformed ports, userinfo, unsupported IP literals (including a hostname whose final label is a WHATWG IPv4 number: all digits, or `0x`/`0X` plus zero or more hex digits), and ambiguous syntax. Match on label boundaries, never arbitrary suffixes. In configuration, host is the base hostname; omitted subdomain matches only the bare host; an exact subdomain = "api" matches only api.base; subdomain = "*" matches any nonempty sequence of subdomain labels but not the bare host.
60	
61	Methods: HTTP tokens, folded to uppercase in rules and requests. RFC 9110 makes them case-sensitive but clients and servers differ, so a request method that folding changes has two readings: folded (all rules eligible) and case-sensitive (only method-less rules eligible). If both name a class and the classes differ, return None; a reading with no rule is not a disagreement. Reject malformed/empty method tokens and values over 32 bytes. Reject configured `method = "*"`: omission, not a wildcard token, means any valid method.
62	
63	Paths: Empty request path normalizes to /; the path portion is capped at 8 KiB after query/fragment removal, and nonempty path must begin /. Drop query/fragment before matching (reject them in patterns). Reject empty segments (`//`) in requests and patterns alike, backslashes, literal semicolons, and non-ASCII or non-graphic bytes; servers can strip `;` path parameters before routing. Keep trailing slashes; for a request ending in `/`, return None when its slash-stripped spelling has a different nonempty classification, because servers can strip the sent slash. Also compare an ASCII-lowercased spelling outside percent escapes against case-folded copies of the configured patterns, and its stripped form; any different nonempty result is rejected to catch common case-insensitive routers without rewriting the normal case-sensitive match. Equally specific rules with different classes matching any spelling (patterns that differ only by case tie once folded) also return None, so rule order cannot decide. `*` in a request path is an ordinary character. Decode only escaped unreserved characters (RFC 3986 6.2.2) and upper-case other escapes, identically for rules and requests; never double-decode. Normalize request dot segments; configured `.` or `..` segments are rejected rather than silently corrected. Reject invalid percent encoding and encoded separators (%2F, %5C). A configured path must start with /; omission matches all valid paths; * matches zero or more characters including /, and multiple wildcards are supported. /v1/refunds/* matches /v1/refunds/ but not /v1/refunds.
64	
65	Loading limits: normalized configured path patterns are capped at 1,024 bytes,
66	a classifier accepts at most 10,000 rules, and all eligible wildcard overlap
67	checks share a 4,000,000-state budget. Unrelated hosts and same-class pairs do
68	not consume this budget; an exhausted budget rejects the load explicitly.
69	
70	Specificity: Lexicographic ranking: (1) host kind (exact/bare over wildcard), then base-host label depth; bare-host rules only match bare host, (2) exact path > wildcard path > absent path; among wildcards, more literal characters > fewer wildcards > longer literal prefix, (3) explicit method > absent method. Mapping base hosts need at least two DNS labels, so a wildcard cannot be rooted at a public-suffix-like single label. Never use file or insertion order to break ties. If any remaining equal-specificity rules could classify the same valid request differently, reject the configuration during load.
71	
72	Important security boundary: Matching URL metadata cannot reveal agent reasoning, authorization, request body, or provider-specific server decoding rules. Do not infer missing information. If normalization is ambiguous, return None for requests or reject the rule when loading. Document important limits.

77	3. How matcher.rs accepts rule data and returns match/specificity results.
78	4. How it checks potential overlap with equal specificity, and how the caller gets enough context to construct errors.
79	5. Error behavior for invalid rules vs invalid request inputs.
80	Agent 1 may compile to a small validated configuration IR; Agent 2 may compile that IR to an internal matching IR. Avoid cyclic imports. A practical dependency direction is config -> normalize for shared validation helpers, then lib orchestrates config and matcher; avoid config <-> matcher cycles. Shared DTO types can live in config.rs or a small model.rs owned by the Integrator.

1	# Take-home: action classifier
2	
3	**Time budget: at most 2 hours of human time.** We expect you to use a coding
4	agent, and we are as interested in the process as in the result.
5	
6	## Context
7	
8	An AI agent's outbound HTTP requests are classified into *action classes*
9	(`payment.refund`, `repo.write`, ...). Policies then allow or deny action
10	classes instead of naming every provider. The classification is driven by
11	**mapping sets**: TOML files that say "requests to this host, method and path
12	are action class X". The caller denies any request the classifier does not
13	classify, so a wrong answer here is a security bug, not a cosmetic one.
14	
15	You will build the classification core as a library. No I/O, network,
16	database or CLI.
17	
18	## What to build
19	
20	Implement the two functions in `src/lib.rs`. Their signatures are fixed;
21	everything else is yours to design.
22	
23	```rust
24	pub async fn load(sets: &[&str]) -> Result<Classifier, LoadError>;
25	impl Classifier { pub async fn classify(&self, method: &str, host: &str, path: &str) -> Option<&str>; }
26	```
27	
28	`load` takes the text of one or more user-provided mapping files. `classify`
29	returns the action class for a request, or `None` when it is unclassified.
30	
31	## Mapping file format
32	
33	```toml
34	format_version = 1
35	name = "Acme Payments"
36	description = "Acme payments API mappings"
37	host = "acme.com"
38	
39	[[rules]]
40	method = "GET"
41	subdomain = "api"
42	path = "/v1/payment_intents"
43	action_class = "payment.read"
44	
45	[[rules]]
46	subdomain = "api"
47	path = "/v1/refunds/*"
48	action_class = "payment.refund"
49	
50	[[rules]]
51	path = "/pricing"
52	action_class = "payment.read"
53	```
54	
55	- A rule applies to the host formed by its `subdomain` followed by the file's
56	  `host`. With `host = "acme.com"`:
57	  - `subdomain = "api"` applies to `api.acme.com`;
58	  - `subdomain = "*"` applies to any subdomain of `acme.com`, such as
59	    `a.acme.com`;
60	  - no `subdomain` applies to `acme.com` itself.
61	- `subdomain`, `method` and `path` are optional. Omitting `method` or `path`
62	  matches everything.
63	- `*` in a path is a wildcard.
64	- `action_class` must be one of `ACTION_CLASSES` in `src/lib.rs`.
65	- Unknown keys are an error, so misspelled keys fail loudly.
66	
67	## Behavior
68	
69	- Both functions will be called from inside an HTTP handler.
70	- When several rules match a request, **the most specific wins**.
71	- Sets are loaded together, with no precedence.
72	- Requests are matched as an HTTP client would send them.
73	- `classify` must never panic.
74	
75	## Deliverables
76	
77	1. The crate, building with no warnings and with `cargo test` passing.
78	2. Your complete AI session transcript, in the most detailed form your tool
79	   offers. Do not summarise, redact or `--sanitize` it. We want to see the
80	   instructions, skills, files and documents you gave the agent, as well as
81	   its tool calls. Send the raw session file, plus the readable export if
82	   your tool has one:
83	   - **Claude Code:** the raw file
84	     `~/.claude/projects/<project>/<session-id>.jsonl` (`<project>` is your
85	     working directory path with every non-alphanumeric character replaced by
86	     `-`; sessions older than 30 days are deleted by default), and
87	     optionally `/export session.txt`.
88	   - **Codex:** the raw file
89	     `~/.codex/sessions/<year>/<month>/<day>/rollout-*.jsonl`, and
90	     optionally `/export session.md`.
91	   - **opencode:** `opencode export <sessionID> > session.json` (run
92	     `opencode export` without an ID to pick the session; do not pass
93	     `--sanitize`).
94	   - If you used several sessions, send all of them. Also send any
95	     instruction files, skills or notes you wrote or installed for the agent
96	     (for example `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, or a `SKILL.md`).
97	
98	We will read your code, your tests and your transcript, then spend about 45
99	minutes discussing them with you.
100
